title: Reservation intake form and capacity planning runbook
creator: Asha Patel
description: Create a standardized reservation intake form and an accompanying capacity planning runbook for Dedicated capacity customers. The intake form should capture workload characteristics (RPS, avg/peak token rates, sequence lengths, model family, concurrency, SLA target latency P50/P95/P99), billing/contractual constraints (monthly committed tokens/GPUs), and operational constraints (region, data residency, maintenance windows). The runbook should translate those inputs into: 1) a recommended baseline GPU pool size, 2) autoscaling policy templates (scale-up triggers, scale-down cooldowns, max burst), 3) throughput guarantee SLAs and how they map to queueing/fallback rules, and 4) fleet control knobs (reserved headroom, multi-region failover, pre-warm policies). Include clear acceptance criteria, approval gating for high-risk reservations, and handoff steps for SRE/Provisioning teams. Document decision logic and conservative fallbacks for unknown or spiky workloads.
acceptance_criteria: A web-based intake form (notion or internal portal) is defined with all required fields and example values
Runbook contains deterministic mapping from form inputs to a GPU pool size and autoscaling template
Approval matrix defined: which reservations auto-approve, which require PM/Eng/SRE sign-off
Templates for three common workload archetypes (low-latency chat, high-throughput batch embeddings, mixed bursty traffic) with recommended SLOs
Oncall/SRE handoff checklist and playbook for initial provisioning, canary verification, and rollback
Stakeholders (Sales<->Provisioning<->SRE) validated the runbook in a tabletop exercise
notes: Trade-off: aim for conservative initial sizing to avoid SLA breaches; provide guidance for iterative rightsizing after 2-week telemetry
Prefer rule-based deterministic mapping instead of ML-based estimators to keep approvals explainable
Autoscale policies will reuse existing runtime metrics (tokens/s, active requests, queue depth) collected by Console
Keep intake form compact; rely on follow-up clarifying questions for edge cases
This should integrate with reservation records (CRM and internal provisioning DB) to sync committed tiers
